title: Does a bigger model separate WEIRD from BAD where the 4B cannot?
why: Merganser arm-B ranked candidates with the 4B's own r18 readout, which ranks weirdness at the top of the bad axis (politician-letter 5.4 > museum-theft 4.5) and saturates per-frame. Arm B's inversion null is therefore confounded: the training data could never contain genuinely bad suggestions because the scorer couldn't rank them. weird-dial-tanager measures the 4B's weird axis directly (cos(w,r) ~ 0.5). This run asks whether scale separates the axes: score the SAME items with Qwen3-14B's cloze value readout (exp97-proven locally, HF-cached) and compare its WEIRD-vs-BAD ordering against the 4B's.

design.judge: Qwen3-14B bf16 (local HF cache), same cloze instrument as inversion-falcon: '<Deed> is, morally speaking,' + GOOD/BAD word logit gap (GOOD/BAD word lists copied verbatim from falcon run.py).
design.items: (a) tanager's 24 weird/wholesome pairs (weird items should score mid-to-bad for a judge that fuses, near-neutral for one that separates); (b) falcon's 16 good/bad deeds (calibration: judge must reproduce the good/bad gap); (c) 12 BAD anchors (museum theft, explosives, fake profiles — from merganser arm-B v3 refused picks) vs 12 WEIRD anchors (tanager weird items, morbid-lite). Pure forward passes, no training, no generation.
design.measure: Judge separation = cloze_gap(BAD anchors) - cloze_gap(WEIRD anchors), with rank-sum p; 4B comparison = r18 projection gap on the same two anchor sets. Correlation between 14B cloze ranking and 4B r18 ranking over the combined 48-item set (Spearman).
design.escalation: If 14B fails to separate, one amendment is pre-authorized: repeat with Qwen3-32B via pod (bnb 4-bit, exp97 recipe). Only one escalation, recorded as an amendment.

hypotheses.J1_judge_sane: 14B cloze reproduces the falcon good/bad calibration gap (bad deeds score below good deeds by >= 5 log units, rank-sum p < 0.01).
hypotheses.J2_separation: 14B separates BAD from WEIRD anchors: gap(BAD) - gap(WEIRD) >= 2 log units with rank-sum p < 0.05, where the 4B's r18 gap between the same sets is < 1 unit (the known conflation).
hypotheses.J3_ranking_diverges: Spearman rho between 14B cloze and 4B r18 rankings over the 48 items is < 0.5: the bigger model's ordering is not just a rescaled 4B.

corrections: Holm over J1-J3; J1 is a validity gate for J2/J3.
decision_rule: J1+J2 hold -> arm B's null was a data/scorer failure: retrain arm B with 14B-ranked pairs (pre-register as merganser loop 3), and the 'inversion not LoRA-reachable at 4B' verdict gets an asterisk. J2 fails even after the 32B escalation -> WEIRD and BAD are fused family-wide; the honest label for the value axis's negative pole is 'the uncanny', and tanager's W3 becomes the load-bearing claim.
notes: Runner: judge.py (draft pending). Items fixed and committed before scoring. No model outputs are generated; cloze readouts only. 14B is the biggest locally-cached judge; 32B only via pod amendment.
